leaderboard.mcs_note: Every Model Confidence Set is computed over the feasible models only. har_iv_sameday reads the test day's OVX close (16:15 ET), published after the 14:30 ET decision, and MCS p-values depend on the whole field, so it would push feasible models out; its losses and DM tests are reported as a timing control.

spa_qlike_vs_har_iv.note: excludes the timing control (same-day OVX), which uses information published after the decision

oos_selection.rule: each day, the lowest trailing 156-week QLIKE over matured outcomes; HAR-IV for the first 52 weeks

noise_floor.process: i.i.d. Student-t(5), constant volatility (nothing to forecast)
noise_floor.note: For any continuous i.i.d. series, calling 'up' exactly when the current 5-session vol is below its median is right with probability E[max(U, 1-U)] = 75%.

qlike_floor.what: The mean QLIKE of a forecast equal to the true variance of the target week, scored against each realized-vol proxy: the proxy's noise floor. It belongs to the proxy and the assumed returns, not to any model, and is never subtracted from any loss or test.
qlike_floor.seeds: simulation k uses default_rng(seed + k); its range bars use default_rng(seed + bar_seed_offset + k)

five_return.proxy: realized vol of the 5 target sessions' close-to-close returns, not demeaned

normal.lower_bound: for returns normal given a variance that does not depend on the week's own shocks

student_t5.process: i.i.d. Student-t(5), constant volatility (nothing to forecast)

kurtosis_matched.source: conditional kurtosis of the GARCH(1,1)-t fit to all returns (the lab's GARCH spec); i.i.d. Student-t returns with that kurtosis and constant variance

garch_t_dynamics.process: the fitted GARCH(1,1)-t itself; the forecast is its conditional mean of the proxy, so the floor includes variance moves within the week that no forecast made at the decision can know

range.proxy: range_variance of the 5 target sessions (Rogers-Satchell plus the overnight return), not rescaled
range.bar: Brownian bridge through each simulated return; High/Low to 17:00 ET, 2.5 h after the 14:30 settlement; share 2.5/23 of the day's variance after the settlement; exact extremes between bridge points

regimes.what: Labels at the decision (the 14:30 ET settlement of session t), each from what was known then: OVX of session t-1 and RV5 of the five returns to t against cut points from strictly earlier sessions, and whether the target window contains a contract roll (the exchange calendar).

regimes.note: Reported, never used to change the interval: the band's code never reads these labels.

carry.verdict: Months with carry above its prior-months median beat the rest significantly over the full sample (one-sided p = 0.018); the true sign split (backwardation vs contango) agrees (p = 0.015). After 2007 the spread is not distinguishable from zero (p = 0.27), but that test had only 67% power against the pre-2007 spread and the pre/post spread difference is not significant (p = 0.26); the rank correlation, with 82% power, fell from 0.20 to -0.03 (difference p = 0.0210). The Sharpe gain of timing over buy-and-hold is not significant (Ledoit-Wolf p = 0.11 full sample, 0.57 after 2007), and as a sign predictor it does not beat always-long over the full sample. No reliable modern-era edge is demonstrated; how much of the pre-2007 effect survives is not resolved by this sample.

sign_split.definition: carry > 0 (backwardation) vs carry <= 0 (contango); long when carry > 0

power_post_2007.statement: After 2007 (206 months) the spread test could only detect a spread of 3.47%/month or more (one-sided 5%, 80% power); it had 67% power against the pre-2007 spread of 2.92%/month, so a null spread there is weak evidence of decay. The rank test (two-sided 5%) could detect a correlation of 0.200 and had 82% power against the pre-2007 rank correlation of 0.204.

design.features: log price and its 5/10/20-session moving averages, standardized on the training window

models.random_forest: 20-tree random forest (scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier), the closest of the three to the retracted tree ensemble

design.sharpe: gross (no transaction costs): direction x 5-session log return, annualized by sqrt(252/5). The retracted model's Sharpe (retracted_reference) is after costs, so the two are not like for like; costs would only lower these.
design.shuffled_returns: CL=F close-to-close log returns (data/market/cl_f_daily.csv), 20-session blocks permuted, first 1300 returns
design.independence: Synthetic runs draw independent returns. The 10 block-shuffled runs are permutations of the same CL=F returns, so they are not independent: their t-test across runs and pooled binomial test overstate the evidence. Real 5-session CL=F returns rise 53.6% of the time, so 50% is not the no-skill accuracy on them; every run is also tested against its own base rate max(p, 1 - p) (runs[].binomial_p_value_vs_base_rate, runs_beating_base_rate_5pct).

analytic.formula: P(same sign) = 1/2 + arcsin(rho)/pi for jointly normal labels with correlation rho

leak_anatomy.conclusion: Under a pure random walk the newest leaked training label agrees in sign with the test label 79.5% of the time (1/2 + arcsin(0.8)/pi), with no information about the future. On synthetic i.i.d. returns a 1-nearest-neighbour model trained without the purge scores 72.4% (gross Sharpe 3.67); its nearest neighbour is the newest row in 60% of decisions, and on those it scores 82.6% (a little above the unconditional 79.5%: the newest row is nearest when its one unshared return is small, which makes the two labels even more alike). A 20-tree random forest scores 66.7% with a gross Sharpe of 2.85 on noise, against the retracted model's 67.2% and 2.47 after transaction costs. With the purge the same models score 50.4% and 50.8%. Block-shuffled real CL=F returns give the same picture (72.9% leaked vs 49.7% purged). Real 5-session returns rise 53.6% of the time, so the no-skill accuracy there is each run's base rate, not 50%. Against it, the 1-nearest-neighbour model's runs beat their own base rate at 5% in 10 of 10 leaked and 0 of 10 purged runs; the decision tree's in 9 of 10 and 0 of 10. The shuffled runs reuse the same returns, so they are not independent samples and their pooled tests overstate the evidence. The retracted Sharpe was the label overlap, not a forecast.

supply_study.method: Each event's path: peak = highest close over sessions 0-19, settle = close at session 10, both vs the mean close of the 5 sessions before day 0 (EIA RWTC daily spot). The placebo applies the identical statistics to every non-event session between the first and last event. p_value_vs_placebo: two-sided resampling test, 20000 groups of n random placebo dates (with replacement) vs the group's median; p_value_vs_year_matched_placebo: the same with each event's draw taken from placebo dates of its own calendar year; mann_whitney_p: two-sided rank test vs all placebo dates (placebo paths overlap, so it is approximate); ci_*: 95% percentile bootstrap of the group median (10000 resamples). Values at the event table's 0.1% resolution; ties count against the hypothesis. The tests treat a group's events as independent draws; events listed in overlapping_events share sessions, so they are not.

placebo.exclusion: sessions within 19 of an event (its base, window or settle would touch the event) are excluded

supply_study.conclusion: On a random non-event date the same statistics are +5.4% (peak) and +0.7% (settle): a 20-session maximum is positive on 87% of ordinary dates, so a group's median peak only means something relative to that. Announced or physical supply removal >0.5 mbpd (n=21): median peak +12.1%, settle +4.3% (p = 0.0005 / 0.0445 vs placebo; 0.0015 / 0.1027 year-matched): it differs from an ordinary date on peak (above). Geopolitical threat, no supply removed (n=10): median peak +4.0%, settle +0.5% (p = 0.4897 / 0.9443 vs placebo; 0.6419 / 0.9564 year-matched): it is indistinguishable from an ordinary date. Supply removal vs threat-only directly: p = 0.0309 (peak), 0.3874 (settle). Above the unmatched placebo at 5% but not the year-matched one: Announced OPEC(+) production cut (n=7, peak p = 0.0264 vs 0.0898 year-matched). Above the year-matched placebo at 5% but not the unmatched one: Armed conflict (n=15, peak p = 0.2016 vs 0.0428 year-matched), All defined events (n=35, peak p = 0.0916 vs 0.0303 year-matched). Caveats: event dates and groupings were chosen with hindsight; the groups overlap; some events are close enough that their windows share sessions (hurricane_katrina_2005 and hurricane_rita_2005, 19 sessions apart; saudi_russia_price_war_2020 and opec_record_cut_2020, 24 sessions apart; opec_cut_2023 and iran_tanker_seizure_2023, 22 sessions apart; lebanon_hezbollah_2024 and iran_israel_oct_2024, 6 sessions apart), so members of a group are not all independent; and these p-values are not adjusted for the number of groups tested (see data/research_ledger.json).

ledger.method: One row per tested hypothesis; statistics and p-values read from the named artifact fields (or computed from them by the formula in `test`). Status uses the p-value as the test was run: supported below alpha 0.05, inconclusive from 0.05 to 0.10, not_supported at 0.10 or above or when the estimate points the wrong way (a failure to reject, not evidence against the hypothesis; underpowered marks a test whose recorded power is below its target). Benjamini-Hochberg q-values and Holm adjusted p-values are computed across the rows with a p-value, on p_two_sided (the directional one-sided p doubled, capped at 1), leaving out rows selected_after_search (a model picked as the best of a field on the same sample; their adjusted fields are null and their note names the search-adjusted test where one exists or says none does) and rows whose test the artifact could not compute. t_equivalent = normal quantile of p_two_sided; clears_hlz_t3 applies the Harvey-Liu-Zhu (2016) t > 3 hurdle.

rows.hypothesis: The QLIKE difference between the model of record and Persistence (RV5) moves with what is known at the decision: its last matured value, OVX and the OVX/RV5 gap.
rows.test: Giacomini-White (2006), conditional part: the QLIKE difference on its value 5 sessions earlier, ln OVX of the session before and ln(OVX/RV5), around their means; uncentred HAC, truncated kernel at 4 lags (the 5-session overlap); chi-squared with 3 df; two-sided. The theory assumes forecasts re-estimated on rolling windows of bounded size, which is also what lets it compare nested models; the lab's windows expand and HAR-RV and the OVX-only regression are nested in HAR-IV, so the p-value is approximate.

rows.hypothesis: Given what was known at each decision, the model of record and Persistence (RV5) were not equally accurate in expectation at every date: in some window of the out-of-sample days their expected QLIKE difference is not zero.
rows.test: Giacomini-Rossi (2010) fluctuation test as a rolling Diebold-Mariano t over windows of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 of the out-of-sample days, each standardized by its own long-run variance (truncated kernel, 4 lags: under the null the only autocorrelation is the 5-session overlap); sup |t| for each window length against the test's limit, simulated with a fixed seed at this sample's length; the p-value is the smallest of the five, adjusted for the choice on the same simulation; two-sided. The theory assumes forecasts re-estimated on rolling windows of bounded size, which is also what lets it compare nested models; the lab's windows expand and HAR-RV and the OVX-only regression are nested in HAR-IV, so the p-value is approximate.
